Hampton Roads Voters Decide Local Races in 2026 Election

  • November 10, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:55
Instaread

Voters across Hampton Roads turned out to settle a range of local contests in the 2026 election, with multiple news outlets tracking returns as they came in on election night. Results spanned city councils, school boards and other municipal offices throughout the region.

According to multiple reports, local outcomes were being tabulated and reported in real time, with several races closely watched and some remaining too close to call as incomplete counts continued into the evening.

Where the results stood

Regional coverage compiled winners across Hampton Roads municipalities, offering a city-by-city look at the outcomes. The roundup of local winners published by WHRO tracked results for communities throughout the area, while statewide tracking from Cardinal News logged returns across Virginia as precincts reported.

As is typical on election night, totals shifted as additional precincts and absentee ballots were counted. Outlets reported that some margins were narrow enough that final results in certain races would depend on the completion of counting.

Suffolk among the closely watched contests

In Suffolk, several local races drew particular attention as officials worked through the count. Early returns in some contests remained too close to call amid an incomplete count, before the picture began to clarify as more votes were tallied and results took shape through the night.

Across the broader region, voters weighed in on a mix of municipal offices and ballot questions, part of the wider slate of decisions Hampton Roads residents faced on 2026 election night.

What to watch next

Local election results typically remain unofficial until canvassing boards certify the totals in the days following the election. Several factors can affect final tallies, including:

  • Outstanding absentee and mail-in ballots still being processed
  • Provisional ballots that require review before they are counted
  • Close margins that could trigger recounts under state rules

Until certification is complete, outcomes in the tightest contests should be treated as preliminary. The specific winners, margins and any races headed for recounts were not uniformly confirmed across the available sources and remain subject to the official canvass.

A regional picture

Taken together, the reporting paints a picture of an active local election across Hampton Roads, with results coming in city by city and statewide trackers logging returns throughout Virginia. Outlets emphasized that live totals were still being updated as counting proceeded.

Readers seeking final, certified outcomes should rely on official results from local registrars and the Virginia Department of Elections once the canvass is complete. In the meantime, the live trackers maintained by regional and statewide outlets offered the most current available snapshot of how Hampton Roads voted in 2026.
